header:
Date: 2026-04-28
Time: 15:00 - 15:55 UTC
Duration: 55 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Blake (Redwood AE), Priya Menon (Redwood SE), Carlos Rivera (Redwood CSM); Maya Chen (Skyline Head of ML), Liam O'Connor (Skyline Head of Platform), Sofia Ramirez (Skyline DevOps), Ethan Park (Skyline Product)
summary: Quarterly business review focusing on usage trends (spike in inference during promotions), cost drivers (large embedding jobs + long context lengths), reliability incidents (two brief outages in March), and roadmap alignment for dedicated capacity and private deployment. Agreed next steps: pricing + sizing, benchmark run, staging access for private pilot, and a technical deep-dive on batching/quantization.
topics: Roadmap: model pinning, rollouts, caching and batching optimizations
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: Alright everyone good afternoon, thanks for joining the QBR. We wanted to walk through usage, costs, reliability, and next steps for the private pilot. I'll hand it over to Maya to start with a quick state of Skyline's usage.

[01:12] Maya: Yep hey thanks Jordan. So the big thing we've seen last quarter was a 3x spike in traffic during the spring promo windows, which sounds great, but it strained our costs. Most of the cost is from long-context generation for product descriptions and a few heavy embedding jobs for search reindexing.

[02:35] Liam: To add, there were two short infra incidents in March where requests timed out for about 10 minutes; root cause I think was a burst exceeding our default autoscale thresholds. We were on hosted endpoints.

[03:10] Priya: Got it, thanks. Do you have the per-route token breakdown? That helps prioritize batching/caching recommendations.

[03:28] Maya: Yeah Carlos sent a condensed report earlier — I'll re-share. The top 3 routes are: generate_product_copy, search_embeddings, and chat_assist. Embedding jobs are the cost outlier.

[04:12] Jordan: Nice, that's consistent with other retail customers. On reliability, the timeouts sound like autoscaling and burst issues — for hosted we can raise autoscale limits or add burst capacity; for Dedicated we can guarantee throughput which avoids this class of outage.

[05:02] Sofia: Quick question — for Dedicated, what's the lead time and how disruptive is migration? We have compliance windows in June.

[05:30] Priya: Lead time depends on sizing but typically 2-4 weeks after agreement for provisioning, longer if you're doing private VPC network setup and HSM/KMS integration. Migration can be staged — you can start with read-only embeddings on Dedicated then flip generation traffic when ready.

[06:12] Ethan: And how different is the API/SDK? We want minimal code changes.

[06:22] Jordan: The API surface is the same — model pinning and routing config are managed on our side, so code changes are usually config-only. There are some optional SDK flags for batching that you can toggle.

[07:05] Liam: On security, SOC2 and SSO are key for us. We need audit logs forwarded to our SIEM and KMS integration so keys are with our provider.

[07:30] Carlos: We support SAML SSO, RBAC roles in console, and can forward audit logs to your S3 or SIEM. For keys we integrate with common KMS/HSM providers; we can share the security pack after.

[08:10] Maya: That would be great; please share the SOC2 and encryption docs. Also, any compliance for data residency in EU? Some store traffic is EU-based.

[08:38] Priya: We have region controls and can pin inference to EU regions; for Private deployments you can manage residency entirely in your VPC. We'll include region/residency notes in the security pack.

[09:25] Jordan: Back to cost — two levers we usually look at: 1) model selection/quantization and 2) batching + KV caching for prefix reuse. For embeddings, quantized models or smaller retriever models often suffice. For generation, shorter max tokens and prefix cache can save a lot.

[10:40] Maya: We tried shortening max tokens, but some merchants need longer context to capture campaign tone. Can Redwood do multi-tier routing so long-context requests hit Dedicated and short ones stay on hosted?

[11:02] Priya: Yes, smart routing by route or token count is supported; we can set policy to route >1k tokens to Dedicated or to a specialized long-context model. There was a small mis-transcribe in our docs where 'KV cache' was spelled 'KV cash' in a sample — sorry about that.

[11:35] Liam: Regarding the outages, do you offer any SLO credits or SLA? Our procurement team will ask.

[11:45] Jordan: For Dedicated we have SLA-backed latency and uptime targets; hosted has a standard availability guarantee and we offer incident postmortems and credits for production incidents above the threshold. We'll include the SLA sheet in the follow-up.

[12:30] Maya: Okay, next I want to talk about the embedding reindex job cost. Is there a way to batch or offload to cheaper instances?

[12:55] Priya: For large batch embedding jobs, we often recommend a dedicated spot fleet or scheduled capacity window — Redwood Dedicated supports burst capacity and cheaper batch pools. Also quantized embedding models can reduce token-time and cost.

[13:40] Ethan: Curious if you support incremental embedding updates so we don't re-run full reindex every time.

[13:50] Priya: Yep, incremental reindexing is supported; you can do delta embeddings for changed items only, and we have hooks to resume partial jobs.

[14:20] Liam: Performance numbers — do you have a baseline for p50/p95 latency for our observed payloads?

[14:32] Priya: From similar retail workloads: p50 around 80-120ms on Dedicated optimized profiles for small generation calls, p95 depends on length and model. For embeddings it's usually under 200ms on optimized quantized variants. But we'll run an exact 24-hour benchmark on your sample traffic to validate.

[15:10] Jordan: Right, that's one of the actions — Priya will run the benchmark using your top-100 queries once you share them.

[15:45] Sofia: For the private pilot we need to prove network connectivity and KMS rotation. Can Redwood support customer-managed NAT and private endpoints?

[16:02] Priya: Yes, private deployment supports VPC peering, private endpoints, and you keep the keys. There are extra ops steps but we've done this for several customers. We'll send a checklist.

[16:40] Maya: What about model versioning and rollbacks? During promotions we might want to A/B test a new model variant.

[17:00] Jordan: Our Console supports canary rollouts and A/B splits, with traffic weighting and automatic fallback policies. You can pin versions at the route level. We'll demo if you'd like.

[17:30] Ethan: That would be useful. Let's add a demo of rollouts into the technical deep-dive.

[18:05] Liam: Billing question — we saw some unexpected overages tied to a misconfigured background job that triggered high-volume embeddings. Any guardrails you recommend?

[18:30] Carlos: We recommend quotas per API key, alerting on token burn rate, and staged deploys for mass jobs. We can set nightly limits for the embedding route and notify when approaching threshold.

[19:00] Maya: Another ask: can you correlate cost per route in the console so our finance team can allocate costs to product lines?

[19:12] Jordan: Yes, Console has token-level cost breakdowns per route and per API key. We'll share screenshots in the follow-up.

[20:00] Priya: Quick note on batching — there's two modes: client-side batching (SDK) and server-side continuous batching. For low-latency retail requests we usually use server-side batching tuned to your p99 latency SLO.

[21:05] Sofia: Do you have recommended batch sizes for our payloads? Some of our calls are tiny, some are big.

[21:22] Priya: We'll tailor after the benchmark, but initial suggestion is to group small requests up to 32 per batch with a max latency cap of 120ms. For larger payloads we minimize batching.

[22:00] Maya: Can Redwood run a cost-savings sim so we can see estimated savings moving to Dedicated plus quantization?

[22:15] Jordan: Yes — we'll run a model using your last 30 days of usage and produce a cost comparison for Hosted vs Dedicated with quantization and batching applied. That's part of the pricing + sizing deliverable.

[23:10] Ethan: Timeline constraints — procurement needs final pricing by mid-May to approve capacity for June.

[23:25] Jordan: Understood, we'll prioritize the pricing spreadsheet and Dedicated sizing.

[24:05] Liam: On the topic of monitoring, we need distributed tracing for request flows into our systems. Does Redwood export traces or integrate with OpenTelemetry?

[24:22] Priya: We integrate with common tracing providers and can emit OpenTelemetry-compatible traces and logs. We'll include a sample instrumented flow.

[25:00] Maya: Any gotchas with the staging env? We saw a mismatch in tokenization between staging and prod once.

[25:18] Priya: Tokenization mismatches usually come from different model versions or tokenizers; we recommend pinning tokenizer version and running sample comparisons. We'll provide a checklist.

[26:05] Jordan: I want to recap the agreed actions so we're aligned. 1) Jordan to share pricing + Dedicated sizing by 2026-05-03. 2) Priya to run 24h benchmark and share results by 2026-05-06. 3) Sofia to provide staging VPC info by 2026-05-05. 4) Maya to send top-100 slow queries and sample prompts by 2026-05-04. 5) Schedule technical deep-dive on batching/quantization and rollout demo (target week of 2026-05-11).

[27:00] Maya: Sounds good. Also please include the SLA and SOC2 pack.

[27:12] Carlos: Will do — I'll attach SOC2, ISO summary, and encryption docs.

[27:30] Ethan: One last minor: are there any limitations around function/tool calling? We rely on tool calling for product taxonomy enrichment.

[27:45] Priya: Function calling is supported; for Private you can host tool endpoints in your VPC. We'll document recommended patterns.

[28:15] Liam: Ok let's talk risks — what could derail the June window?

[28:25] Jordan: Main risks: delayed staging access, procurement timing, and any unexpected security review blockers. If staging access is late, we can still do a hosted benchmark but it won't validate VPC networking.

[29:05] Maya: We'll prioritize getting staging access. Procurement will push back on any SLA that's not firm.

[29:30] Jordan: We'll include clear milestones in the pricing doc to help procurement.

[30:00] Priya: Anything else on roadmap? We plan to release improved quantization profiles and a more granular cost breakdown in Console next quarter.

[30:18] Maya: Happy to beta the granular cost breakdown if it helps.

[30:30] Jordan: Great, we'll sign you up.

[31:05] Sofia: Quick nit — we've seen small transcription errors in Redwood invoice line items in the Console export; is that something you track?

[31:20] Carlos: We can look into the export parsing. Please send an example and we'll correct it.

[32:00] Ethan: On A/B testing, can we route 10% of traffic to a cheaper quantized model for non-critical routes and measure user impact?

[32:12] Priya: Absolutely; Console supports route-level splits and metric collection for rollouts. We'll help instrument the metrics you care about.

[32:45] Liam: Ok let's confirm the follow-up meeting cadence — a technical deep-dive week of 2026-05-11 and a procurement check-in mid-May?

[33:00] Jordan: Yes, we'll send calendar invites after the benchmark results.

[33:30] Maya: Thanks everyone, that was productive.

[33:40] Jordan: Thank you — we'll share the docs and pricing. Closeout?

[33:50] Maya: Close.

[34:00] [End of recording — transcription continues with lower confidence lines omitted due to silence/clipping.]
